findings.description: The new Assert-ManagedTargetContained check is called only by Set-ManagedFile. Other mutators in the same shipped script bypass it: Ensure-Directory calls New-Item, Write-MissingFile and Set-ManagedBlock/Set-ManagedTableRows call WriteAllText, and host-skill cleanup calls Remove-Item. A consumer-controlled .squad or host-skill ancestor junction can therefore redirect init/update directory creation, team/routing/history writes, or cleanup into an external directory even though runtime-file writes now fail closed. Apply the same component-wise containment check before every read or mutation, including directory creation and deletion.
findings.title: Canonical deployment still mutates through linked ancestors

findings.description: Get-ContinuousCoReviewPathCaseSensitive flips probeDir's own leaf and treats an enumerated flipped spelling as proof that two distinct directories exist. It never verifies that the caller's original spelling is also enumerated, and it measures lookup in the parent rather than lookup inside probeDir. On a case-insensitive parent where the real entry is REPO but the caller supplied repo, REPO is listed and the function incorrectly returns case-sensitive; a Windows case-sensitive project directory under an insensitive parent is misclassified in the opposite direction. The resulting comparer can re-open case-alias containment bypasses or collapse distinct candidate paths. Probe semantics inside the physical target and distinguish one aliased entry from two actual siblings.
findings.title: The case-sensitivity probe can misclassify the target directory

findings.description: The source-hash maps were changed to ordinal dictionaries, but their before/after key union is still built with Sort-Object -Unique -CaseSensitive. CaseSensitive does not make Sort-Object ordinal; culture-equivalent but byte-distinct Git names, such as composed and decomposed Unicode spellings on a case-sensitive filesystem, can still collapse. If only the discarded path is modified, Test-GitReviewTargetSnapshotIntegrity never compares it and can report intact. The same pattern is also used in the verification integrity loop and in exclusion/machinery normalization. Deduplicate with a HashSet using the same ordinal or volume-derived comparer as the maps, and sort only for presentation.
findings.title: Integrity path unions still use culture-aware uniqueness

findings.description: The --host/--authorization-ref path constructs a fresh default reviewer catalog, then preserves only existing rows that are both allowed and authorized, and only copies allowed, authorization_ref, and model from those rows before replacing the whole file. Re-authorizing one host therefore resets that host's pinned model when --model is omitted and drops unrelated row fields or deliberate non-allowed suspension references. This can silently destroy reviewer identity and independence policy. Update only the addressed row's authorization_ref (and explicitly supplied model), preserving every other field and row from the existing file.
findings.title: Recording one reviewer grant rewrites unrelated host policy

summary: Risk-based review completed. Both controller-declared verification commands succeeded against the exact target digest, but four major defects remain in managed deployment containment, filesystem case detection, path-manifest uniqueness, and reviewer authorization persistence.
